name: Kettlebell Reverse Lunge
description: With the kettlebell held in the rack (or goblet) position, step one leg straight back and lower until both knees bend to roughly 90 degrees, back knee toward the floor. Keep the torso tall and the core braced, front knee tracking over the toes. Drive through the front heel to return to standing. The reverse step is easier on the knees than a forward lunge and keeps the front foot planted for a stronger, more stable drive. When racked on one side, the offset load also challenges anti-lateral-flexion of the trunk.
